messages:
Raj (AcmeCorp): Hey team — our Private deployment (VPC) started failing calls to Redwood yesterday after our infra team rolled an SSL profile on the corp outbound proxy. App logs show TLS handshakes failing. Error from our side: 'SSL handshake failed: no shared cipher'. Can you advise?

Alice Nguyen: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the exact curl/openssl output you see and the proxy vendor/version? Also confirm whether your service cert is RSA or ECDSA.

Raj (AcmeCorp): Curl output (sanitized):
```
$ curl -v https://private-api.redwood.example/v1/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private-api.redwood.example/v1/health
*   Trying 10.1.2.3...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to private-api.redwood.example (10.1.2.3) port 443 (#0)
* schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: Unknown error (0x80092012) - The revocation function was unable to check revocation for the certificate.
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake failed
```
And openssl (from a bastion inside the VPC):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood.example:443 -servername private-api.redwood.example -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' -msg
CONNECTED(00000003)
139761234567872:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:s23_clnt.c:770:
---
no peer certificate
---
```
Proxy: F5 BIG-IP 13.1 with a custom SSL profile pushed last night (managed by corp-net). Certificate on our side is ECDSA (Let's Encrypt).

Tom H.: Thanks — two quick thoughts: 1) If the proxy strips or disallows ECDHE/ECDSA ciphers, a client presenting ECDHE + ECDSA won't find a shared cipher with a proxy that only allows RSA key exchange. 2) TLS1.3 always uses ECDHE; if the proxy disables curves or TLS1.3 support, connections will fail.

Priya SRE: Can you run an openssl probe that lists server-supported ciphers from the proxy path? Also run from the same host: `openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood.example:443 -tlsextdebug -status` and capture the raw handshake. If you can also grab a tcpdump of the initial handshake (port 443) that helps.

Raj (AcmeCorp): Pasted the proxy SSL profile cipher string from corp-net: `DEFAULT:!ECDHE:!ECDSA:!TLSv1.3` (yikes). They also set an explicit curve list to empty. Here's what our infra sees when probing the proxy endpoint (proxy terminating TLS then re-encrypting to upstream):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect corp-proxy.egress:443 -servername private-api.redwood.example -cipher ALL -msg
---
read:errno=0
139761234567872:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1544:
```

Alice Nguyen: That cipher string explains it. If the proxy is explicitly disabling ECDHE and ECDSA and also disabling TLS1.3, it will not be able to proxy traffic where the backend or client requires ECDHE/ECDSA (Let's Encrypt ECDSA certs or modern clients). Two remediation paths:
- Short term: Ask corp-net to allow ECDHE ciphers and at least the curves used by your cert (prime256v1 / secp384r1). Also allow TLS1.2 ECDHE and TLS1.3 if possible.
- Short term workaround: If corp policy prohibits ECDHE, switch the backend certificate to an RSA-signed cert (so RSA key exchange and RSA signatures are available). That requires re-issuance and likely a maintenance window.
- Medium term: Configure a dedicated egress route for Redwood traffic that bypasses the proxy or uses an allowlist to keep the proxy from re-writing TLS.

Tom H.: For debugging, please run from the bastion: `openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood.example:443 -servername private-api.redwood.example -cipher 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' -msg -tlsextdebug` and also try forcing RSA ciphers to see behaviour: `-cipher 'AES128-SHA'`. If RSA ciphers succeed but ECDHE fail, that confirms the proxy is stripping EC suites.

Raj (AcmeCorp): Ran those. ECDHE probes fail; RSA probe returns TLS1.2 handshake but server cert then fails validation because our server sticks with ECDSA cert. So we see either no shared cipher or cert/signature algorithm mismatch.

Priya SRE: Quick note on why TLS1.3 matters: TLS1.3 doesn't use the traditional cipher-suite names — if the proxy blocks TLS1.3, you lose modern handshake behavior. Many proxies that edit ClientHello (for policy) will break modern clients. If corp-net cannot enable ECDHE for policy reasons, the only robust option is to terminate TLS downstream of the proxy (i.e., have the proxy do TCP passthrough) or present an RSA-backed cert at the proxy and re-encrypt to your backend (not ideal for end-to-end crypto).

Alice Nguyen: We can escalate this with our infra/compatibility docs. From Redwood's side, we recommend:
- Allow these curves: prime256v1,secp384r1.
- Allow these ciphers at minimum: `ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`, `ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384` and TLS1.3.
- If proxy is an F5, ask them to not use `!ECDHE` in the cipher string and to not clear the curve list.

Raj (AcmeCorp): I'll open a ticket with corp-net and get them to allow the curves. In the meantime, is there anything Redwood support can do to accept the proxy behavior so our app doesn't break?

Tom H.: From Redwood's hosted side, we can't change your corp proxy. We can suggest a graceful retry/backoff or route via a different egress region if your infra allows it. If you have a Dedicated/Private appliance with control over the edge, you can switch to RSA cert to temporarily restore connectivity.

ingress-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0458 — "Corp proxy cipher policy causing TLS handshake failures for AcmeCorp private deployment". Assigned to support-L2.

Alice Nguyen: Thanks Raj — please share the corp-net ticket number and the proxy SSL profile (cipher string + curve list + TLS protocol blacklist). We'll keep this ticket open and coordinate with SRE if an infra escalation is needed.

Raj (AcmeCorp): Will do, ticket CN-5921 created. I'll share updates here once corp-net responds. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

Tom H.: Marking this thread for follow-up. If corp-net allows ECDHE and the problem persists, collect the tcpdump pcap (first 2-3 round trips) and pastebin the openssl debug output.

(End of thread)
